- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to align with sentiment momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.67) or volatile, model often overpredicts; reduce forecast to reflect pessimism or correction pressure.  
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., 30d forecast spikes to 7+ after 2.35–2.37 history), leading to overshoot; cap or dampen forecasts after 3 consecutive high sentiment days.  
- Mean reversion is evident: model often forecasts 1–2 days below true value after strong upward moves; adjust downward by 10–20% if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.  
- For 30d horizon, model underestimates true values when sentiment is consistently positive; apply a +0.1 to +0.3 offset to forecast if sentiment > 0.67 for 5+ consecutive days.  
- If sentiment history shows rapid shifts (e.g., 0.67 → -0.67 → 0.67), model often misjudges direction; use 3-day moving average of sentiment to smooth forecast bias.
